messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall-lee — routing_anomaly detected: latency-steering policy triggered mass failover from eu-west to ap-south, elevated 5xx and p95. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (hosted). See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fallbacks

pagerduty: Paging oncall-lee (primary) — created INC-5151239, severity SEV2.

oncall-lee: Acked. Pulling traces, recent policy changes, and canary history. Adding alex-sre and nina-net.

alex-sre: I'm in. I see a policy evaluation job ran at 03:07 UTC that recalculated weights based on probe signals. Candidate applied weight for fallback (eu->ap-south) = 95 (intended 30). Looks like a units mismatch in the autoscaler output.

ops-bot: policy-change: deploy/latency-steer v2 -> v3 by nina-net at 2026-06-12T03:07:12Z commit ee9a7f.

nina-net: Confirming I pushed the change but unit tests passed. Investigating why deploy system accepted 95. Canary showed slight uptick in probe fail but not obvious.

oncall-lee: Symptoms: 10-18% 5xx for EU customers, p95 latency 2.3s -> 9.8s for some routes. Visible queuing on ap-south upstreams. Customer impact: multiple EU tenants experienced transient failures and higher latencies. Claire, can we get a short customer impact note?

claire-pm: Short note: "Users in EU observed degraded response times and intermittent failures for API requests to text endpoints. We're applying mitigations and will follow up with a detailed postmortem." Happy to circulate.

oncall-lee: Immediate mitigations: 1) apply emergency cap to fallback weight (max 50) 2) pin eu regions to local preference while we roll back 3) throttle new policy evaluations. I'll run commands.

```
$ routectl set-policy-cap global max_fallback_weight=50 --reason "emergency cap"
apply: success
```

ops-bot: policy-cap applied by oncall-lee.

```
$ routectl set-override eu-west pin=80 duration=20m reason="mitigate cross-region shift"
override: applied
```

ops-bot: override applied: eu-west pin=80 (20m) by oncall-lee.

alex-sre: After cap + override we see error rate fall from ~15% -> ~3% over next 4 minutes. Latency p95 trend returning toward baseline.

nina-net: I'm preparing a rollback to deploy/latency-steer@ee9a7f~1 (previous working commit). Will apply to control-plane.

```
$ git checkout ee9a7f~1 && routectl apply /policies/latency-steer.yaml
apply: success
```

ops-bot: policy rollback complete. Current policy weight fallback eu->ap-south = 30, ttl=20s.

oncall-lee: Good. We'll keep override until confidence high. Maria (not on thread) — can you run a customer sweep to identify all impacted tenants and attach logs? Alex, please capture a short timeline and save traces to INC-5151239.

alex-sre: Will do, capturing span IDs and sample traces. Noted that ap-south cluster saw CPU ~92% during the spike which explains 502s.

claire-pm: Drafting outbound comms: planned brief to affected customers in next 30m. Also will prepare a follow-up template for postmortem.

oncall-lee: Follow-ups/live tasks: 1) root cause: investigate units mismatch in autoscaler output -> INF-3301 2) add safety check: reject fallback weight > 70 in policy controller -> INF-3302 3) add canary alert for abrupt weight jumps -> INF-3303. Assign to eng-runtime + eng-platform.

nina-net: For immediate prevention I'm opening a control-plane validation PR to block weight values > 70 unless overridden by a human.

oncall-lee: On-call handoff: I'll stay watching for 15m, then hand to alex-sre as primary for post-incident tasks. Leaving override duration 20m.

ops-bot: override expiry scheduled at 5151241078 (20m).

incident-bot: INC-5151239 status update: mitigation in place, customer impact reduced to minimal. Severity remains SEV2 while we validate. Add timeline and action items to the incident ticket.

claire-pm: Customer impact summary for notes: 5-18% of requests for a subset of EU tenants returned errors during 03:07-03:20 UTC; no data loss. We mitigated via emergency caps, regional override, and policy rollback. Next step: postmortem w/ root cause and remediation.

oncall-lee: Thanks team. I'll publish a short status note to #incidents and close the paging. Leaving this thread open for postmortem updates. :thumbsup:"
